title: Efficient Turing Machine Simulation with Transformers
claim: A queue is equivalent to a cyclically shifting tape, and a hierarchy of sized queues can emulate a stack efficiently.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line; left stacked equivalence, right level rows
description: The figure has two parts divided by a vertical dashed line. On the left, a Queue drawn as a box (b3 | b4…bn-1 bn b1 b2) is paired with a Tape box (b1 b2 | b3 | b4…bn-1 bn) through a double-headed vertical arrow. Annotations mark 'Read then delete' at the queue front and 'add' b3' at the back. A blue triangle under the tape marks the head, with the caption 'shifting one cell to the right cyclically at each step'. On the right, rows labelled Lv 1, Lv 2 and Lv k' each show a left/right queue pair (Q'_{i,L}, Q'_{i,R}) and a separate buffer queue Q'_{i,B}. Cells hold symbols or blank ⊥ symbols, with dashed dividers. Blue braces mark each queue's capacity, from s^{1/k'} up to s^{k'/k'} = s. Vertical dots between rows show the hierarchy continues. The figure is black and white with blue accents.
caption: \warn{Left: A queue can be viewed as a tape with the head shifting one cell to the right cyclically at each step. Right: Illustration of the queues to simulate a stack.}
abstract: Constant bit-size Transformers are known to be Turing complete, but existing constructions require $Î©(s(n))$ chain-of-thought (CoT) steps per simulated Turing machine (TM) step, leading to impractical reasoning lengths. In this paper, we significantly reduce this efficiency gap by proving that any $(t(n),s(n))$-bounded multi-tape TM can be simulated by a constant bit-size Transformer with an optimal $O(s(n))$-long context window and only $O(s(n)^c)$ CoT steps per TM step, where $c>0$ can be made arbitrarily small by letting the Transformers' head-layer product sufficiently large. In addition, our construction shows that sparse attention with fixed geometric offsets suffices for efficient universal computation. Our proof leverages multi-queue TMs as a bridge. The main technical novelty is a more efficient simulation of multi-tape TMs by synchronous multi-queue TMs, improving both time and space complexity under stricter model assumptions.
